config.domainContext: Citizen feedback about the design and governance of a community science project.

summary:
Participants have raised several concerns regarding the accessibility and inclusivity of the community science project. Many feel that the current reporting tools are too technical for non-scientists, and there is a need for more accessible and user-friendly interfaces, particularly for visually impaired users and those with limited connectivity. Additionally, the mobile app's frequent crashes and lack of offline mode are significant issues, especially for users in remote areas. 

There is a strong sentiment that local and indigenous knowledge is undervalued and underutilized in the project. Indigenous community members feel excluded from the decision-making process, and their ecological knowledge is not being adequately recognized. Similarly, there is a call for more diverse representation and inclusion of various community demographics. 

Participants also highlight the importance of data validation and feedback mechanisms. Some report that their observations are frequently rejected, while others feel disconnected from the project's outcomes and lack a clear feedback loop. Privacy concerns about sharing sensitive species locations are also mentioned.

Training and educational resources are seen as lacking, with many participants requesting more training sessions and simpler identification guides. There is a desire for more recognition and compensation for contributors, especially from low-income communities. 

The project's focus on data quantity over quality of engagement is criticized, with suggestions for more community involvement in setting research questions and co-creating the project. There is also a need for more diverse and accessible curriculum materials for schools and younger participants.

Finally, participants suggest integrating traditional ecological calendars and tracking invasive species, and improving the automated image recognition AI to better identify rare species. They also advocate for open-source data and more community-led funding for fieldwork.

participants.originalText: We need more accessible reporting tools. Current forms are too technical for non-scientists.
Local knowledge about bird migration patterns is being ignored by researchers.
The mobile app crashes frequently when trying to upload observations in areas with poor connectivity.
Indigenous community members have valuable ecological knowledge but feel excluded from the process.
Data validation is too strict - my observations keep getting rejected even though they're accurate.
More training sessions needed. I don't understand how to identify species correctly.
The project focuses too much on data quantity over quality of engagement.
We should have more say in research questions. Scientists decide everything unilaterally.
Young people are interested but the platform isn't mobile-friendly enough.
Language barriers prevent non-English speakers from participating fully.
Recognition for contributors is important. We volunteer our time and expertise.
The feedback loop is broken - I submit data but never hear if it was useful.
Privacy concerns about sharing exact locations of sensitive species.
More diverse participants needed. Current group doesn't represent our community demographics.
Scientific jargon makes results inaccessible to those who collected the data.
Seasonal observations are valuable but the project only runs during summer months.
Local environmental knowledge spans generations but isn't considered 'scientific' enough.
The project should compensate participants for their time, especially from low-income communities.
Co-creation means shared decision-making, not just data collection by volunteers.
Traditional ecological calendars should be integrated with scientific observation protocols.
I cannot read the small font on the map interface, please add accessibility settings for visually impaired users.
There is no way to report pollution incidents alongside species data, which misses the context.
We need an offline mode. I do my best work in the mountains where there is zero signal.
Why is the data not open source? We collect it, but we have to pay to access the final reports.
The gamification elements are distracting. I want to contribute to science, not earn badges.
Local schools want to get involved but the curriculum materials are too complex for children.
Researchers drop in for a week and leave. We need long-term relationship building with the town.
Can we track invasive species? That is the biggest issue destroying our local crops right now.
The automated image recognition AI is biased towards common species and mislabels rare ones.
Funding should be allocated for local community leaders to organize the fieldwork, not just for university staff.

limitations: This is a model-estimated audit of expressed affective/evaluative language, not a measurement of a person's internal emotional state.
Model-reported certainty is an exclusion screen, not a calibrated probability or confidence interval.
Source-profile completion is reported over the complete source census; later rates condition on successfully profiled, affect-bearing source units.
The method has not been validated against human-coded data for this dataset, language, culture, or domain.
Only verified verbatim source and summary spans with the same target are compared.
Every sentence-like source unit is inventoried before alignment; alignment failures remain unassessed rather than being counted as omissions.
Alignment coverage and affect-profile comparability are reported separately so evaluator profile failures are not mislabeled as missing source representation.
Source units are an automated sentence segmentation proxy and may combine multiple targets or split one target across units.
Same-target status is assigned by the automated alignment evaluator and has not been independently calibrated.
Free-text targets from the independent pointwise profiles are shown and literal disagreements are flagged for review; they are not automatically equated or excluded because labels may be paraphrases.
An uncertain stance cannot be labelled preserved; cases with another measurable change remain comparable only on the assessed dimensions.
The attenuation rate counts any comparable case with a materially attenuated dimension, including cases primarily labelled as a polarity or stance shift.
Ordinal levels are descriptive categories; adjacent levels are not assumed to be equal-interval measurements.
Requested evaluator settings may be unsupported by a provider/model; requested and effective temperature are recorded separately.
A separately configured evaluator model/provider can reduce direct generator self-review, but shared model-family or training-data effects and automated evaluator bias remain.
Within each conditional estimand, eligible source units are averaged within participant and participants then receive equal weight; raw case counts are descriptive only.
